- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- Model often lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lag in sentiment-driven momentum.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.67), model shows mean-reversion bias; forecast should be closer to recent 7-day average, not 30-day average.  
- In high volatility periods (e.g., 2024-12-02), model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days after sentiment spikes.
